Here, $R_x \in SO(3)$ is the spatial rotation matrix, $\text{diag}(\mathbf{s}_x)$ is a $3 \times 3$ diagonal matrix of spatial scales, $\mathbf{0}_{3 \times C}$ is a zero matrix, $\mathbf{L}_{qx}$ encodes correlations between spatial and non-spatial dimensions, and $\mathbf{L}_q$ is a lower-triangular matrix for the non-spatial subspace [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately describes the components of the structured lower-triangular matrix $L$ as defined in Source [S1]. Specifically, [S1] defines $L = L_{qx} L_q$ where the top-left block is $R_x diag(s_x)$ (with $R_x$ being a spatial rotation matrix in $SO(3)$ and $diag(s_x)$ being a diagonal matrix of spatial scales), the top-right block is a zero matrix ($0$), the bottom-left block $L_{qx}$ encodes cross-dimensional (spatial and non-spatial) correlations, and the bottom-right block $L_q$ is described as part of the Cholesky factorization for the remaining dimensions. While the claim states $L_q$ is 'lower-triangular', [S1] describes the overall matrix $L$ as 'structured lower-triangular' and $L_q$ as the factor for the non-spatial subspace in a Cholesky decomposition ($L_q L_q^T$), which implies $L_q$ is lower-triangular in the context of the Cholesky factorization for that subspace. All specific facts mentioned in the claim are present and consistent with the evidence provided in [S1].
